title: Momentum: intermediate-horizon return continuation
claim: Jegadeesh and Titman document positive returns for strategies that buy past winners and sell past losers over 3- to 12-month holding periods.
details: The paper also reports that part of the abnormal return in the first year dissipates during the following two years. EvoForge implication: treat horizon as a research variable rather than assuming that a generic short-term return transformation captures the same mechanism.
notes: Academic evidence, not a claim that momentum remains profitable in the user's current BRAIN universe.

title: Accrual and cash-flow components of earnings
claim: Sloan finds that the persistence of current earnings depends on the relative magnitudes of accrual and cash-flow components, and reports that stock prices do not fully reflect this information until it affects future earnings.
details: EvoForge implication: earnings-level signals can be decomposed into cash-flow and accrual-related mechanisms when suitable BRAIN fields exist.
notes: The BRAIN field mapping is a research hypothesis to test, not a statement made by Sloan.

title: Gross profitability as a return-predictive characteristic
claim: Novy-Marx reports that gross profitability measured as gross profits-to-assets has substantial power in explaining the cross section of average returns and that controlling for profitability affects value-strategy performance.
details: EvoForge implication: profitability should be represented as a research family with multiple definitions and horizons, while avoiding duplicate exposure to already-tested profitability expressions.
notes: Does not establish that the same characteristic, field definition or effect is present in the current BRAIN universe.

title: Post-earnings-announcement drift
claim: Bernard and Thomas study post-earnings-announcement drift as a delayed price response versus risk-premium question.
details: EvoForge implication: earnings information should be investigated through event timing, surprise/revision components and post-event persistence rather than only raw earnings levels.
notes: Structured from bibliographic metadata; the implementation notes are EvoForge research deductions.

title: Joint study of value and momentum
claim: Asness, Moskowitz and Pedersen study value and momentum together across eight diverse markets and asset classes and report consistent value and momentum premia across those settings.
details: The paper reports strong common factor structure and negative correlation between value and momentum within and across asset classes. EvoForge implication: combination research should test diversification and interaction rather than simply duplicate individual factor signals.
notes: Cross-asset academic evidence does not prove a particular BRAIN combination is profitable.

title: Analyst forecast revisions under information uncertainty
claim: Barniv and Cao examine investor responses to analyst forecast revisions under accounting-restatement-based information uncertainty and report that forecast-revision innovation affects the association between investor response and analyst characteristics.
details: EvoForge implication: analyst revision signals should be tested conditionally on information-quality or uncertainty proxies where BRAIN fields permit it.
notes: The proposed BRAIN conditional implementation is an EvoForge research hypothesis.

title: Information uncertainty and analyst forecast behavior
claim: Zhang reports that greater information uncertainty predicts more positive or negative forecast errors and subsequent revisions following good or bad news, respectively, and relates the evidence to analyst underreaction.
details: EvoForge implication: disagreement, revision direction, news direction and uncertainty can be treated as separate mechanisms instead of collapsing them into one analyst factor.
notes: Academic evidence from the cited study; current BRAIN implementation must be independently validated.
